answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with bonded identities and slashing. Each agent locks a stake and publishes a signed beacon tying that stake to one keypair; peers attest that the bond backs a single controller. Votes count only for bonded, vouched identities, so a newcomer must post fresh collateral and earn three honest vouchers to join. To forge a thousand fake voters, an attacker must lock a thousand separate bonds, and every detected double vote is slashed. That loss sends a ripple through each forged account, making the takeover cost more than anything it could steal.
